# CareerAIR — make the action-required notification actually actionable
# guidance: WO-YYYY-MM-DD-nn — slice title

## Acceptance criteria

AC1. A message that states a candidate deadline, or requires a candidate action (assessment, test,
     interview scheduling, document request, offer response), classifies as `action-required` — not
     `needs-warwick-review`. Proven by unit tests over real captured shapes, including the Veeva
     "Next Steps"/Rembrandt shape, which is the known miss.
AC2. For an `action-required` item, the CareerAIRbot card names the employer, the role, the required
     action, the deadline where the source states one, and the link. A count-only card fails AC2.
AC3. The narrowed leak guard is scoped: the cockpit sink, all non-action-required classes, and
     failure cards are UNCHANGED and still throw on personal data. Proven by a test that asserts the
     guard still fires on those paths.
AC4. Mutation-proven: break the enrichment and the card silently reverts to counts — the test must go
     RED with a non-zero executed count, and the source digest must be shown to have changed between
     runs. Restore; GREEN with a non-zero count. A control that can pass by doing nothing is not a
     control.
AC5. NOT EXECUTABLE BY KEEL, and must not be claimed: proven by a REAL SCHEDULED RUN publishing an
     enriched card. Larry executes and evidences this after integration. Capability is not automation.
# guidance: each independently checkable. If automatic, no AC may be satisfiable by a manual invocation of the delivered script alone.
